column1: # The shared boundary tests (tests/boundary.py), in this language: up and down are the script a case becomes, @V@ the value written here, @ID@ the case. A case with no v: line is one this language cannot write. @NL@ is a newline.
# The other direction (tests/boundary.py run-invoke): scripts that export commands for the host to call. x:make returns @V@; x:back hands its argument back.

column2: set n 0@NL@proc count {} { incr ::n }@NL@proc boom {} { error boom }@NL@export count boom
proc big {} { string repeat x 100000 }@NL@export big
for {set i 0} {$i < 300} {incr i} { proc f$i {} [list return $i]; export f$i }

set pending [list [txn_start deposit] [txn_start refund]]@NL@set seen 0@NL@proc on_txn {id} {@NL@    set d [txn_details $id]@NL@    incr ::seen@NL@    return "$::seen [dict get $d kind] [dict get $d amount]"@NL@}@NL@export on_txn
proc pick {a b c} { return $b }@NL@export pick
